values: AMR-109-0151 (11000151): Wajnryb Artin A5 quotient question

Fixed-generator positive factorizations in Wajnryb's Artin A5 quotient — Alec Kriebel (ORCID0009-0001-9320-500X), v1.0. Preprint date: 2026-10-03. Complete fixed-standard-generator classification: lengths20/30/40 with1/1/2 strict Hurwitz classes; simultaneous conjugation gives three classes. Classical group presentation, prior numerical spectrum and Casson crossing assertion credited; historical first priority not certified. Six-page unrefereed preprint; extensive AI use, no external human peer review. Two sequential fresh adversarial review rounds completed; first required package repair fixed, second found no mandatory issue. PDF plus full source/verification ZIP includes all810 actions, all90921 records and both independent backward controls. Primary question: https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~farb/papers/mcgbook.pdf, Wajnryb Section3, printed126 of linked online version. Record: https://zenodo.org/records/23124601. Reviewed PR: https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/pull/367.
Maximum Central Points in Cube-Move alpha-Immersions / OWR-2654831-006 (30004563)

Five outgoing centers in a 16-realization cube move (PR193). Six fixed algebraic boundary points admit an incoming center and at least five distinct outgoing centers, refuting the at-most-three expectation of Melotti–Ramassamy–Thévenin, Remark4.8, in the realization setting allowing crossings. Exact rational bounds and symbolic face identities; fixed crossing excludes proper embeddings. Exact total, universal maximum and alpha<1 are outside scope. Earlier weighted-distance/p-power families of Ash–Bolker, Bourne–Peletier–Roper and Bourne–Roper credited. Bounded search found no earlier four-or-more pure-power witness in its checked corpus; historical priority and firstness remain unestablished. Two new independent whole-package adversarial reviews clean. Extensive AI; unrefereed; no conventional human peer review.

records.title: Fixed-generator positive factorizations in Wajnryb's Artin A5 quotient
records.description: We classify positive words in the five fixed standard generators of B6 modulo c=h representing c^2. The possible lengths are 20, 30 and 40, with respectively one, one and two strict Hurwitz classes. Simultaneous conjugation identifies the two length-40 classes, giving the three proposed representatives of Wajnryb's quotient question. A pure-braid linking reduction and an exhaustive exact 810-word certificate settle length 20. The classical group presentation, previously known length spectrum and Casson's twice-per-pair crossing assertion reported by Elrifai-Morton are explicitly credited. A full reproducible six-strand crossing certificate and independent controls accompany the note. Novelty of the exact complete classification is not certified by a negative literature search. AI tools were used extensively in solving, verifying, literature research, writing and adversarial review. This is an unrefereed preprint and has not received external human peer review. The statement is restricted to fixed-generator input words, not arbitrary conjugate-factor or geometric factorizations.

records.title: Five outgoing centers in a 16-realization cube move
records.description: This note specifies six fixed algebraic boundary points admitting an incoming alpha=16 realization and at least five distinct outgoing centers. Exact rational bounds, the intermediate value theorem and monotone polynomial root definitions prove the construction. It contradicts the at-most-three expectation in Melotti–Ramassamy–Thévenin (2023), Remark 4.8, in the realization setting allowing crossings. A fixed boundary crossing excludes proper embeddings. The exact total count and universal maximum remain unknown. The curves are members of the earlier weighted-distance and p-power families of Ash–Bolker (1986), Bourne–Peletier–Roper (2014) and Bourne–Roper (2015). A bounded search through 15 October 2026 located no earlier pure-power four-or-more shared-focus example in its checked corpus; historical priority remains unestablished. AI was used extensively. This preprint is unrefereed and has not received conventional human peer review.
